title: Trouble Calling MCMC Multiple Times within Same Script
author: mlpotter

comments.author: GStechschulte
comments.body:
Hey @mlpotter, this is interesting. I know you said script, but just to make sure, you are running this class within a Python script (the main program being executed) and **not** a Jupyter Notebook correct? 

I had a similar problem, though not the same, when running MCMC with $> 1$ chains in a Jupyter Notebook. My error was also being thrown in the `multiprocessing` directory, albeit, with the `spawn.py` file. Here's the [link](https://forum.pyro.ai/t/attribute-error-when-setting-number-of-chains-greater-than-1-in-mcmc/4652) to my problem on the Pyro forum.

comments.author: mlpotter
comments.body:
The main program being executed is not a Jupyter Notebook. I am importing into a script like main.py. 

I resolved the threadlock error by adding in main.py file `if __name__ == "__main__":`.

When running the same script in Windows, I received a pickling error that commonly appears in this issue boards with this code 

```
 def fit(self,X_train,X_val,y_train,y_val,t1_train,t1_val,t2_train,t2_val):
        self.nuts_kernel = NUTS(self.model)

        self.mcmc = MCMC(self.nuts_kernel,
                         num_chains=self.num_chains,
                         num_samples=self.number_of_samples,
                         warmup_steps=self.burn_in_samples,mp_context='spawn')

        trace = poutine.trace(self.model).get_trace(X_train,t1_train,t2_train,y_train)
        trace.compute_log_prob()
        print(trace.format_shapes())

        self.mcmc.run(X_train, t1_train, t2_train, y_train)
```

But was able to resolve it by removing self assignments and adding a self assignment at the end of fit.

```
def fit(self,X_train,X_val,y_train,y_val,t1_train,t1_val,t2_train,t2_val):
        nuts_kernel = NUTS(self.model) 

        mcmc = MCMC(nuts_kernel, 
                         num_chains=self.num_chains,
                         num_samples=self.number_of_samples,
                         warmup_steps=self.burn_in_samples,mp_context='spawn')

        trace = poutine.trace(self.model).get_trace(X_train,t1_train,t2_train,y_train)
        trace.compute_log_prob()
        print(trace.format_shapes())

        mcmc.run(X_train, t1_train, t2_train, y_train) 
        self.mcmc = mcmc # making the self statement at end after mcmc run does not give error
```
